text:
nadia: Heads-up — we're getting a handful of production misses where requests should route to tenant-specific models but fall back to the default pool. Likely header spoofing or UA-based heuristics kicking in. Thinking we need a signed header from the edge to assert tenant identity.

chris: Can you paste a quick example of the failure pattern? Is it always `x-customer-id` missing or sometimes `User-Agent` mismatch?

nadia: It's a mix. Example: internal metrics show 502 -> fallback route for ~0.2% of requests. In traces we see `x-customer-id` present but different downstream because some proxies rewrite headers. UA-only routing gets used for a subset of older SDKs.

alex: Hmm. Header rewrite by proxies is real. We should prefer auth-derived identity (JWT `sub` / `azp`) when available, then signed edge header, then the x-customer header, and finally UA heuristics as last resort. Order matters for quotas and billing.

lee: +1 on auth-first. But not all clients send JWT (embedded devices). For those, signed header from edge (edge signs `x-rdwd-tenant` with HMAC) would give us integrity. Edge could drop unsigned tenant headers.

sam: What about latency and key rotation? If edge signs every request we need a cheap HMAC operation — trivial — but rotation needs coordination with private deployments.

infra-bot: deploy-job:deploy-edge-signer started by @lee — status: queued.

chris: Prototype idea: envoy filter (lua) that injects `x-rdwd-tenant` and `x-rdwd-tenant-sig` on ingress. We validate sig in gateway service before routing. Pseudocode: 

```
local tenant = get_header("x-customer-id")
local sig = HMAC(secret, tenant + path + timestamp)
set_header("x-rdwd-tenant", tenant)
set_header("x-rdwd-tenant-sig", sig)
```

nadia: Nice. Add `timestamp` TTL to avoid reuse. And make gateway double-check keystore cache with async refresh to avoid per-request KMS calls.

lee: For private deployments, we can allow customers to bring their own signer or trust a local CA. We should document the option in Private README.

sam: How do we handle legacy clients that only send UA and we can't sign? UA heuristics are brittle and cause noisy routing. Maybe map UA to a low-confidence route and always place them under a throttled quota or isolate in a canary pool.

chris: Agree — mark UA-derived routing as "heuristic" in telemetry. Add a metric `route_resolution_confidence` with values {auth, signed_header, header, ua, unknown}.

nadia: Ops asks: if gateway rejects unsigned `x-customer-id`, do we 403 or route to default? Security prefers 403. Business prefers default (less disruption). Suggest making it configurable per customer: strict (403) / permissive (default).

lee: Configurable per-tenant makes sense. UI in Console can be a checkbox for strict header enforcement. Also expose a rollout toggle (canary 1% -> 100%).

alex: We also need to avoid header spoofing for billing. If a client tries to set `x-customer-id` to a higher-tier account, signed header prevents that. Good win.

sam: One more: ensure we preserve the original client `User-Agent` for downstream app logic (don't overwrite). Signed header should be additive and not mutate client headers except when dropping unsafe ones.

nadia: I'll draft an RFC with: precedence rules, signed-header format (tenant, ts, sig, version), k/v for per-tenant strictness, telemetry fields, and an Envoy filter prototype. I'll drop it in eng-platform RFCs.

chris: Thanks — ping me when the draft is up, I'll review the telemetry bits. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-job:deploy-edge-signer queued -> running

lee: Quick test plan idea: create synthetic clients that attempt header spoofing and UA-only clients, validate routing and metrics, then enable strict mode on staging.

nadia: Perfect. Target RFC today, prototype by EOD tomorrow.

alex: One tiny nit: ensure that when routing falls back (unknown) we tag traces with `routing.fallback_reason` so we can run queries like `count by fallback_reason`.

nadia: Good call. Adding that to the RFC checklist.

chris: 👍
